findings.proposedChange:
Three module-level additions beside `load()` (scripts/test_account_workflows.py:173), then a rewritten `_case_statuses` body.

ADD immediately above `def load(path):` at line 173:

# The `case "$verdict" in` opener, as a WORD: `case` and `in` must not be the
# tails of longer words. Matched against comment-stripped text and confirmed
# against the mask, so neither a comment nor a string can supply it.
_CASE_VERDICT = re.compile(r'(?<![\w.-])case\s+"\$verdict"\s+in(?![\w.-])')

# Everything that can change where one `case` arm ends: the two block keywords
# as WORDS, and bash's three arm terminators.
_CASE_TOKEN = re.compile(r'(?<![\w.-])(?:case|esac)(?![\w.-])|;;&|;;|;&')


def _mask_quoted(text):
    """`text` with every QUOTED character blanked out, same length.

    The counterpart to `_uncomment`, and the same three-state walk: `'...'`,
    `"..."`, and a backslash escaping the next character everywhere except
    inside single quotes. It answers the one question a scan over shell has to
    be able to ask - is this `;;`, this `esac`, this `|` CODE OR DATA - and it
    answers it without pretending to be a bash parser.

    Blanking rather than deleting, and newlines left alone, so the result is
    the same LENGTH as its input and every index found in the mask indexes the
    original: patterns are always sliced out of the text, never out of this.

    `shlex` is the obvious alternative and is the wrong tool twice over. It
    REMOVES quotes, and the distinction between `"$drift"` and `$drift` is
    exactly what test_the_case_block_names_every_status_the_module_knows
    exists to assert - an unquoted expansion is re-read as a pattern, so a
    glob in the constant would silence every verdict. It also has no notion of
    a `case` pattern, so `*[!A-Za-z0-9]*` and `''|*)` are not words to it.

    It models what `_uncomment` models and no more; see that docstring for the
    two approximations. Callers here hand it ONE comment-stripped `case`
    block, where a heredoc cannot appear and no string is left open.
    """
    out = list(text)
    quote = None
    i = 0
    while i < len(text):
        ch = text[i]
        if ch == "\\" and quote != "'":
            if quote:
                out[i] = " "
                if i + 1 < len(text) and text[i + 1] != "\n":
                    out[i + 1] = " "
            i += 2
            continue
        if quote:
            if ch != "\n":
                out[i] = " "
            if ch == quote:
                quote = None
        elif ch in "'\"":
            out[i] = " "
            quote = ch
        i += 1
    return "".join(out)


def _unquote(token):
    """One `case` pattern with a symmetric pair of surrounding quotes removed.

    `"fresh"`, `'fresh'` and `fresh` are one pattern to bash. Only ever
    applied to a LITERAL - see the caller for why an expansion keeps its
    quotes.
    """
    if len(token) >= 2 and token[0] == token[-1] and token[0] in "\"'":
        return token[1:-1]
    return token

THEN REPLACE the whole body of `_case_statuses` (scripts/test_account_workflows.py:1076-1109, from `body = self._body()` through `return body, literals, variables`) with:

        body = self._body()
        # COMMENTS FIRST, with the file's own quote-aware stripper, because
        # every delimiter below is a delimiter only when it is CODE. A `#`
        # comment that happens to contain `;;` split an arm in half and turned
        # the comment's tail into a "pattern"; one containing `esac` ended the
        # block early and lost every arm after it. Stripping after the split
        # cannot help - by then the comment has already been cut in two.
        text = code(body)
        mask = _mask_quoted(text)
        # The opener no longer has to be a line of its own. That anchor existed
        # to stop `body.index` from following a COMMENT that quotes the opener
        # verbatim, and comments are gone by here; the mask covers the other
        # half, a quoted occurrence. What the anchor also did was reject
        # `case "$verdict" in <first arm>)` on one line - the form
        # record-account-upload.yml:59 and :78 both ship - with "the opener is
        # no longer a line of its own", which is a red on a reformat that
        # changes nothing bash can see.
        opener = next(
            (m for m in _CASE_VERDICT.finditer(text)
             if mask[m.start():m.start() + 4] == "case"), None)
        assert opener, (
            "the audit step's `case \"$verdict\" in` is no longer a command "
            "this test can find; it no longer knows which block it is reading"
        )
        # ONE WALK, OVER THE MASK, COUNTING NESTING. `esac` closes THIS block
        # only at depth 0, so a nested `case` in an arm body no longer ends it;
        # `\besac\b` rather than a substring, so `esacapade` does not either;
        # and both are read off the mask, so an `esac` inside a `::warning::`
        # string is data. All three arm terminators, because bash has three:
        # `;;` ends an arm, `;&` falls through to the next arm's body and `;;&`
        # goes on testing patterns.
        depth, start, spans, closer = 0, opener.end(), [], None
        for m in _CASE_TOKEN.finditer(mask, opener.end()):
            token = m.group(0)
            if token == "case":
                depth += 1
            elif token == "esac":
                if depth == 0:
                    closer = m.start()
                    break
                depth -= 1
            elif depth == 0:
                spans.append((start, m.start()))
                start = m.end()
        assert closer is not None, (
            "the audit step's `case` has no closing `esac` outside a string "
            "and outside a nested `case`; this test cannot tell where the "
            "block ends, so its arms would be counted as absent"
        )
        spans.append((start, closer))
        literals, variables = set(), set()
        for begin, end in spans:
            arm, armmask = text[begin:end], mask[begin:end]
            if not arm.strip():
                continue
            # The FIRST UNQUOTED `)`, off the mask: a `)` inside a quoted arm
            # body is not where the pattern ends.
            cut = armmask.find(")")
            assert cut != -1, (
                "an arm of the audit step's `case` has no pattern this test "
                f"can read, so its statuses were counted as absent:\n"
                f"{arm.strip()}"
            )
            pattern, patternmask = arm[:cut], armmask[:cut]
            bars = [i for i, ch in enumerate(patternmask) if ch == "|"]
            prev = 0
            for i in bars + [len(pattern)]:
                token = pattern[prev:i].strip()
                prev = i + 1
                # A POSIX leading `(` is punctuation, not part of the first
                # pattern: `(fresh|unavailable|"$drift")` names `fresh`.
                if token.startswith("("):
                    token = token[1:].strip()
                # QUOTES ARE STRIPPED FROM A LITERAL AND KEPT ON AN EXPANSION,
                # and the asymmetry is the point. `"fresh"` and `fresh` are the
                # same pattern to bash, so the set comparison must not tell
                # them apart; `"$drift"` and `$drift` are NOT the same pattern,
                # and the assertion below exists to require the quoted one.
                if "$" in token:
                    variables.add(token)
                else:
                    literals.add(_unquote(token))
        return body, literals, variables

The docstring above `body = self._body()` (lines 1050-1075) keeps its history paragraphs but its two false claims need editing: "split on `;;`" is no longer what it does, and "the way bash does" should become the honest statement of scope — quote-aware, comment-free, nesting-counted, and explicitly NOT a bash parser (no heredocs, no `esac` reached through a variable, no extglob).

THE ONE-CHARACTER TRAP, stated because it cost a full cycle here: `(variables if "$" in token else literals).add(_unquote(token))` looks like a faithful port of the current line 1108 and is WRONG — it unquotes `"$drift"` to `$drift` and reds every single shape including the control, with the misleading message "the quiet arm no longer matches the drift verdict through exactly one quoted expansion". Write it as the explicit if/else above.

findings.evidence:
Measured or reasoned against the candidate implementation:
- `_mask_quoted` tracks quotes across the whole comment-stripped block, not per line as `_uncomment` does. That is correct for a `case` block and wrong for a heredoc body; callers hand it a case block only.
- The `case` keyword is counted as a nesting opener on a word match alone. `echo case` unquoted in an arm body would increment depth and the block's real `esac` would then be read as the nested closer. Not present today; would fail LOUD ("no closing esac") rather than silently.
- extglob patterns (`@(a|b)`), an `esac` reached through a variable, and a `case` whose word is built by expansion are all outside the model. Each fails loud.
- `code(body)` inherits `_uncomment`'s two documented approximations. Both fail toward DROPPING text, and dropping cannot invent a `case`, an `esac` or a `;;` — the safe direction, and the same argument that docstring already makes.
- For FINDING 3, `[:space:]` in the C locale is space/\t/\n/\v/\f/\r, which matches Python's str.strip() over ASCII. A non-ASCII Unicode space would be stripped by Python and not by the shell. Not reachable: the value comes from skills-evals' `freshness_verdict`, whose vocabulary is seven ASCII words.
findings.proposedChange: Put this list in the `_mask_quoted` docstring and in the PR body, in the same voice the file already uses for `_uncomment`'s "WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT MODEL" paragraph. The claim to make is "quote-aware, comment-free, nesting-counted", never "the way bash does" — the current `_case_statuses` docstring makes the second claim and that overstatement is part of what let six shapes through.

openQuestions: Should the boundary walk be factored into ONE shared helper used by both `_case_statuses` and `_guard`, rather than the two near-copies specified above? Two call sites is the threshold where a shared `_shell_block(text, mask, opener_regex) -> (start, end, spans)` stops being a premature abstraction and starts being the thing that keeps them from drifting apart — which is exactly how they drifted into two different unanchored scanners in the first place. I specified them separately so each diff is reviewable on its own; say which you want before implementation.

Does the fix to `_case_statuses` want to also RELAX the opener anchor, or only the closer? I specified relaxing both (the anchor's stated purpose — stopping `body.index` from following a comment — is served strictly better by stripping comments first, and keeping it means a reformat toward record-account-upload.yml:59/:78's shipped one-line style reds the suite). But that anchor is load-bearing prose in the current docstring and dropping it is the one part of this change that removes a guard rather than adding one.

Is `not-yet-bootstrapped` reachable with trailing whitespace in a way that matters? With the FINDING 3 trim, ` not-yet-bootstrapped` now reaches its own arm and raises the conditional fresh-install annotation, where today it reaches `*)` and raises the vocabulary-moved one. Both annotate, so no run goes from loud to quiet — but the annotation TEXT changes for that input, and if anyone is grepping run logs for the old wording it moves under them.

Should FINDING 2 and FINDING 3 be one PR or two? They touch different files (test helper vs workflow) and have independent verifiers, but they are the same underlying defect — a shell construct read by something that is not a shell — and the AGENTS.md 'one logical change per commit' rule cuts both ways here.

The eight `_ARMS_OK` fixtures need a home. I specified them as a module-level list inside test_account_workflows.py built by an in-memory `_splice()`. The alternative — committed fixture workflow files under a tests/fixtures/ dir — would be more readable but adds files to a repo whose CI globs `plugins/*/skills/*/tests/`, and would need its own salient-path entry. I recommend in-memory; confirm.
